question: GQ-001
subject: the silent no-op edit — the defect behind five of today's failures
the_defect: An edit that does not apply while the patch script exits 0 AND node --check passes. Five times today a comment satisfied a guard meant for code; the fifth was inside my own patch script, where a comment I had just added contained the string I was guarding on, so the import was silently skipped.

reproduced_in_isolation.why_it_matters: both signals said success. A no-op edit is indistinguishable from an applied one unless something checks the RESULT.

the_rule: state what must be true AFTER the edit and verify it against the file on disk, not against the string you built in memory

failure_modes_all_verified.result: throws by default; count:3 applies deliberately

proven_on_the_real_case: ensureImport lands the import into a file whose COMMENT already contains the module name — the exact input where my original guard skipped it. 2 imports on disk, symbol reachable as code.

a_wrong_test_i_caught.what: I asserted 'a' was an ambiguous anchor in 'export const a = 1;'
a_wrong_test_i_caught.reality: it occurs exactly ONCE — the helper was right and my test was wrong
a_wrong_test_i_caught.lesson: I asserted a count instead of deriving it, inside a test written to catch asserted counts

also: removed a dead heredoc I left in the new probe; the probe still passes, which is what proves it was unused
